large vision-language models (LVLMs) (OpenAI, 2023; Liu et al., 2023a; Bai
et al., 2023; Huang et al., 2023; Chen et al., 2023a; Hu et al., 2024b; Chen
g.title: N1 [Context] (cites=9) Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) has emerged as a promising direction in large vision-language models (LVLMs) (OpenAI, 2023; Liu et al., 2023a; Bai et al., 2023; Huang et al., 2023; Chen et al., 2023a; Hu et al., 2024b; Chen et al., 2024; Tong et al., 2024; McKinzie et al., 2024).

g.text: By incorporating external knowledge during generation, models such as
Wiki-LLaVA (Caffagni et al., 2024) have demonstrated improved performance in
g.title: N2 [Prior_Work] (cites=1) By incorporating external knowledge during generation, models such as Wiki-LLaVA (Caffagni et al., 2024) have demonstrated improved performance in knowledge-intensive question answering tasks.

g.text: There are several existing benchmarks evaluating retrieval-augmented LVLMs.
g.title: N3 [Prior_Work] (cites=0) There are several existing benchmarks evaluating retrieval-augmented LVLMs.

g.text: For example, OK-VQA (Marino et al., 2019) focused on scenarios where the
image content alone is insufficient to answer the questions.
g.title: N4 [Prior_Work] (cites=1) For example, OK-VQA (Marino et al., 2019) focused on scenarios where the image content alone is insufficient to answer the questions.

g.text: A-OKVQA (Schwenk et al., 2022) further extended this dataset to incorporate
g.title: N5 [Prior_Work] (cites=1) A-OKVQA (Schwenk et al., 2022) further extended this dataset to incorporate additional types of world knowledge.

g.text: More recent works (Chang et al., 2022; Chen et al., 2023b; Mensink et al.,
2023) further expanded and curated large-scale knowledge base data to
evaluate pre-trained vision and language models in knowledge-intensive and
g.title: N6 [Prior_Work] (cites=3) More recent works (Chang et al., 2022; Chen et al., 2023b; Mensink et al., 2023) further expanded and curated large-scale knowledge base data to evaluate pre-trained vision and language models in knowledge-intensive and information-seeking visual questions.

g.text: However, as shown in Table 1, these benchmarks remain text-centric, as their
questions can often be resolved with related external textual knowledge.

retrieving text, as humans often gain greater insights from it.

g.text: In this paper, we introduce MRAG-BENCH, a benchmark specifically designed
for vision-centric evaluation for retrieval-augmented multimodal models,
with visual questions typically benefit more from retrieving visual
g.title: N11 [Method] (cites=0) In this paper, we introduce MRAG-BENCH, a benchmark specifically designed for vision-centric evaluation for retrieval-augmented multimodal models, with visual questions typically benefit more from retrieving visual knowledge than textual information.

g.text: MRAG-BENCH consists of 16,130 images and 1,353 human-annotated multi-choice
g.title: N12 [Method] (cites=0) MRAG-BENCH consists of 16,130 images and 1,353 human-annotated multi-choice questions spanning 9 distinctive scenarios.

g.text: Focusing on utilizing visually augmented knowledge in real-world scenarios,
we divide our benchmark into two aspects: perspective, where changes in
visual entity's perspective requiring visually augmented knowledge; and
g.title: N13 [Method] (cites=0) Focusing on utilizing visually augmented knowledge in real-world scenarios, we divide our benchmark into two aspects: perspective, where changes in visual entity's perspective requiring visually augmented knowledge; and transformative, where the visual entity undergoes transformative change physically thus requiring visually augmented knowledge.

g.text: Specifically, MRAG-BENCH requires models to reason about visual entities
that undergo perspective changes, such as angle, partial, scope and
occlusion, as well as transformative changes, such as temporal, incomplete,
g.title: N14 [Method] (cites=0) Specifically, MRAG-BENCH requires models to reason about visual entities that undergo perspective changes, such as angle, partial, scope and occlusion, as well as transformative changes, such as temporal, incomplete, biological and deformations.

g.text: Additionally, MRAG-BENCH includes 9,673 human-selected images, which serves
as the ground-truth image knowledge corpus for model evaluation.
g.title: N15 [Method] (cites=0) Additionally, MRAG-BENCH includes 9,673 human-selected images, which serves as the ground-truth image knowledge corpus for model evaluation.

g.text: We conduct extensive experiments on MRAG-BENCH to evaluate 10 open-source
g.title: N16 [Result] (cites=0) We conduct extensive experiments on MRAG-BENCH to evaluate 10 open-source and 4 proprietary LVLMs.

g.text: The results confirm that MRAG-BENCH is vision-centric, as all LVLMs show
greater improvements when augmented with images compared to textual
g.title: N17 [Result] (cites=0) The results confirm that MRAG-BENCH is vision-centric, as all LVLMs show greater improvements when augmented with images compared to textual knowledge.

g.text: Our results indicate that the best-performing GPT-4o model only achieve
68.68% and 74.5% of accuracy without RAG knowledge and with ground-truth
g.title: N18 [Result] (cites=0) Our results indicate that the best-performing GPT-4o model only achieve 68.68% and 74.5% of accuracy without RAG knowledge and with ground-truth (GT) RAG knowledge, respectively.

g.text: This substantially outperforms the best open-source model LLaVA-OneVision by
g.title: N19 [Result] (cites=0) This substantially outperforms the best open-source model LLaVA-OneVision by 15.39% and 15.52%, respectively.

g.text: Notably, we observe while all models improve with GT knowledge, only
proprietary models are able to effectively utilize noisy retrieved
g.title: N20 [Result] (cites=0) Notably, we observe while all models improve with GT knowledge, only proprietary models are able to effectively utilize noisy retrieved multimodal knowledge.

g.text: This indicates the gap between open-source and close-source models still
g.title: N21 [Result] (cites=0) This indicates the gap between open-source and close-source models still exists.

g.text: Open-source models are falling short on their parametric knowledge and the
ability to distinguish between high-quality and poor-quality retrieved
g.title: N22 [Result] (cites=0) Open-source models are falling short on their parametric knowledge and the ability to distinguish between high-quality and poor-quality retrieved visually augmented examples.

g.text: In comparison to humans, GPT-4o achieves only a 5.82% improvement when
augmented with GT knowledge and 0.28% with retrieved knowledge, whereas
humans demonstrate a 33.16% and 22.91% improvement, respectively.
g.title: N23 [Result] (cites=0) In comparison to humans, GPT-4o achieves only a 5.82% improvement when augmented with GT knowledge and 0.28% with retrieved knowledge, whereas humans demonstrate a 33.16% and 22.91% improvement, respectively.

g.text: These results highlight the importance of MRAG-BENCH in encouraging the
community to develop LVLMs better utilizing of visually augmented knowledge.
g.title: N24 [Contribution] (cites=0) These results highlight the importance of MRAG-BENCH in encouraging the community to develop LVLMs better utilizing of visually augmented knowledge.
